1.why: Wavelength is the distance between two consecutive wave crests.

wrong.c: Wind speed affects generation, not wavelength definition.
wrong.d: Water depth affects wave shape, not wavelength itself.

2.why: Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz), meaning cycles per second.

3.why: Multiply frequency (0.5) by wavelength (4) to get 2.0 m/s.

wrong.a: 0.125 comes from division or wrong math.

_quiz_pool.question: What does wavelength measure?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Wavelength is the distance from one crest to the next.

_quiz_pool.question: What is the unit of wave speed v?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Speed is distance divided by time, measured in m/s.

_quiz_pool.question: If frequency increases while wavelength stays constant, wave speed...
_quiz_pool.explanation: Speed is directly proportional to frequency.

_quiz_pool.question: What drives the formation of wind chop on the ocean?
options: Friction from wind blowing across the water surface
_quiz_pool.explanation: Wind friction transfers energy to the water surface.

_quiz_pool.question: What does frequency f measure?
options: Waves passing a point per second
_quiz_pool.explanation: Frequency counts cycles per second in hertz.

_quiz_pool.question: In deep water, long ocean swells travel...
What is 1 hertz equal to?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Hertz is defined as cycles per second.

_quiz_pool.question: Why do ocean waves slow down near the coast?
options: Water becomes shallow and interacts with the seabed
_quiz_pool.explanation: Shallow water seabed friction slows wave progression.

_quiz_pool.question: Which wave property is represented by lambda (λ)?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Lambda is the Greek letter used for wavelength.

_quiz_pool.question: What is transferred across the ocean by a wave?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Waves transport energy without permanently moving water mass forward.

story.title: When wind meets the open sea
story.lead: Strong winds blowing across the ocean transfer energy into the water, creating rhythmic waves that roll toward the shore [1].
story.image_caption: Archive photo · Cascading waves at Kallbadhuset Lysekil
stat.1.label: wave frequency in hertz (Hz)
stat.2.label: wavelength in metres (m)
stat.3.label: wave speed in metres per second (m/s)
story.body_1: When steady winds blow across the water surface, friction pushes the water into ripples and growing waves [2]. As wind speed increases, these waves gather energy and travel across vast ocean basins toward coastal regions [1].
story.body_2: When waves reach shallow coastal waters, their speed changes and they rise higher before breaking on the shore [3]. Understanding how wave speed depends on frequency and wavelength helps scientists track coastal safety.
timeline.1.text: Wind transfers energy to the water surface, building waves.
timeline.2.text: Waves propagate across the sea carrying kinetic energy.
timeline.3.text: Waves slow down in shallow water and break on the shore.
physics.title: How fast do waves travel?
physics.body_1: A wave moves energy through water without carrying the water itself far away. The speed of a wave depends on how frequently the waves pass by and the distance between wave crests.
physics.body_2: We calculate wave speed, v, by multiplying the wave frequency, f, by the wavelength, λ. Higher frequency or longer wavelength means greater speed.
physics.assumptions: We assume regular sinusoidal waves travelling in deep water without energy loss.

lab.step_1: Fill a shallow tray with water and let it settle.
lab.step_2: Tap one end gently with your finger once per second to make ripples.
lab.step_3: Observe how fast the ripples move across the tray.
